title: Tea(m)Time-Studie – Qualitativer Teil -Implementation conditions and mechanisms of action
summary:
Background
In healthcare facilities, such as hospitals, working conditions are constantly changing. For example, demographic shifts, shortages of skilled workers, and changes in legislation are leading to increasingly complex working conditions in hospitals, which can affect all professional groups. Various factors, such as those outlined here, can lead to psychological stress in everyday work. To prevent this psychological stress, implementing health promotion interventions is a suitable approach. To provide solid evidence of their effectiveness, it is necessary to scientifically monitor and evaluate these interventions. As part of the Tea(m)Time study, in addition to measuring effectiveness (quantitative part, Clinical Trials: NCT06694584; OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/VBYP4), an evaluation of the implementation conditions and the mechanisms of action (qualitative part) is being conducted.

Objective:
Through focus group interviews with various stakeholders who, as users or practitioners, have gained experience with the Tea(m)Time method as part of the intervention, we seek to answer the following research questions:
- Research Question A: From the stakeholders’ perspective, what are the mechanisms of action of the Tea(m)Time intervention?
- Research Question B: From the stakeholders’ perspective, which factors related to the implementation of the Tea(m)Time intervention are perceived as hindering or facilitating?

Methodology
Up to seven focus group interviews, conducted by an interviewer using an interview guide, are recorded on audio devices and subsequently transcribed, yielding transcripts that form the basis of the analysis.
- To address Research Question A, the Realistic Review method developed by Pawson & Tilley is applied.
- To answer research question B, the transcripts will be analyzed using the Framework Analysis method developed by Ritchie & Spencer.
conditions: This study examines the implementation and dissemination conditions, as well as the mechanisms of action, of the Tea(m)Time intervention, which is designed to promote resilience and a sense of psychological empowerment among hospital staff.

interventions.name: As part of this qualitative study, we are interviewing users of the Tea(m)Time intervention who participated in the program as part of standard Organisational Development (OD) at a clinic, and thus not as part of the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Participation in the intervention 
- 18 years of age or older
- Clinic employee
- Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
- Did not participate in the intervention
- Under 18 years of age
- Not a clinic employee
- Insufficient knowledge of German
